subject.title: Browser-heavy sessions block all main lanes — need dedicated browser lane or per-channel lane routing

question: Should OpenClaw add a public scheduler/config contract for isolating browser-heavy, channel-specific, or workload-classified foreground turns from fast message replies, and what shape should that contract take?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the solution adds public lane-routing semantics across core scheduler, config, channels, browser automation, and adjacent per-agent proposals, so automation should not choose that product contract.

options.title: Design unified scheduler lanes
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved lane classification model that can cover browser, channel, agent-group, and priority use cases while keeping `main` as the default and preserving an aggregate safety cap.

options.title: Narrow to browser isolation
options.body: Add a smaller browser-workload lane first, accepting that per-channel and per-agent starvation may remain separate follow-up decisions.

options.title: Fold into per-agent scheduler work
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43235 as the broader design vehicle and keep this issue as browser/workload evidence rather than a separate implementation path.

recommendation.title: Design unified scheduler lanes
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved lane classification model that can cover browser, channel, agent-group, and priority use cases while keeping `main` as the default and preserving an aggregate safety cap.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-history signal for the central lane resolver, gateway lane setup, and foreground main-lane path points to Peter Steinberger-authored commits.
